If the question is meant to ask the best way for any random person to die, I would have to say that asphyxiation with nitrogen or some other inert gas would be best. We know that the human urge to breathe - the reason that you'll start to freak out if you're smothering in tight, stuffy place - is not primarily tied to the amount of oxygen in the blood, but rather the amount of CO2. This means that if somebody breathes an atmosphere that's dense enough that it feels normal, and allows for CO2 to leave the blood, but doesn't have enough oxygen to sustain consciousness, they tend to pass out without much distress.

This is a serious hazard for people in tight environments underground or in aircraft at high altitude, so we have a lot of data from people who purposefully or accidentally went through the experience. Almost universally, these people experience a clouding of thought and even a bit of euphoria. Most of the time, they don't even notice what's happening unless they've specifically had training to detect and combat hypoxia.

Compare this to the sort of struggling and agony that we see when we look at popular methods of execution - except for methods where the procedure is specifically altered to prevent the condemned from being able to struggle or express suffering, such as lethal injections where we actually kill somebody with one of the most brutish and painful toxins we have, but only after completely paralyzing them with a separate drug. (What a fucking horror show, honestly.)

So, if somebody's got to die, that's how it should be done, frankly. Execution can be done that way (if it has to be done at all), the terminally ill should be given that option to go out on their own terms, et cetera...

Now, if you're asking about my personal preference, if I can't choose the above option when old age eventually catches up to me, I'd choose to either be shot through the heart in a climactic battle between good and evil, or killed in the midst of indulging some freaky-deaky fantasy.
